newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Integrated Technology of Israel plans IPO.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Technology of Israel plans IPO.

text.p: Jerusalem-based Integrated Technology USA Inc (ITI) is expected to hold an initial public offering (IPO) of approximately $18 million on the American Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

The company, a maker of voice communications hardware for the Internet and computer/telephony applications, plans to offer 3.0 million shares of common stock and an equivalent number of warrants at a price of about $6 a share and $0.10 a warrant, at the lower end of the prospectus estimate.
The offering is for 40 percent of equity. Underwriters, led by National Security Corp, have an option to take an additional 450,000 each of shares and warrants.
Among its products is CompuNet 2000, an integrated PC keyboard and telephone that enables conferencing between an Internet and conventional phone call.
ITI lost $1.7 million on sales of $804,000 in 1995 and showed a loss of $871,000 in first-half 1996 on sales of $208,000.
ITI is a U.S. registered company but conducts most of its activities is Israel.
